Definition: a prolonged form of a primary verb (obsolete except in certain tenses as an alternative of this) of uncertain affinity; to push (as wind, oars or dæmonical power):--carry, drive, row.
BiblicalUsage: The word elaúnō carries the sense of to drive, to row. In Mark 6:48, the text says "And he saw them toiling in rowing." In Luke 8:29, the text says "and was driven of the devil into the wilderness."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that elaúnō matters because creation is God's handiwork, and it still speaks of Him to anyone willing to look. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
